critique.paragraph: The map reads as a sparse exhibition floor rather than a teaching plate. Edge D requires visible sorting, categorization, and exclusion—a Vesalius-cousin diagram where the unlabeled region becomes the argument. This space has the grid infrastructure (pink lines suggesting measurement, categorization) but no central artifact demonstrating what the algorithm fails to see. The scattered dots in the corner hint at data points but don't construct a legible claim about representational silence. A player would cross this room without encountering the edge spatially.
strengths: Dark surface provides negative space for contrast
Scattered elements (if data points) gesture toward categorization
weaknesses: No teaching artifact that demonstrates representational silence
No sorting mechanism, labeled categories, or exclusion visible
Too sparse to function as a Haeckel-style diagram-as-argument
Player path encounters no spatial claim about what algorithms don't see
Missing the frame-in-frame or labeled-diagram-with-gap pattern
next_gen_hints: Add central sorting artifact: a classifier with labeled bins where the player category is conspicuously absent
Use Vesalius pattern: place a detailed anatomical/typological diagram with one region deliberately unlabeled or greyed out
Show feature extraction visually: pedestals measuring height, color, shape—with visible gaps in what's measured
Position unlabeled silhouette or data point at path center, surrounded by fully-labeled examples
Consider boolean-cut vocabulary: show the positive space of categories, make the excluded region a literal void
Add weight: the plate should be dense enough to read as diagram, not empty stage
